subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep the current fallback behavior after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repository policy treats fallback behavior and auth/provider routing as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or operator-visible warning behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split visibility after proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation portion after live proof and track fallback visibility as a narrower follow-up issue.

options.title: Accept logged fallback
options.body: Maintain the current log-level fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or operator-visible warning behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across auth-profile storage, OpenAI provider identity, Codex bridge behavior, and subagent/session routing.
